title: REST API with a database, auth and tests
summary: A backend service with a relational database, user authentication, input validation and an automated integration test suite, running in Docker.
why: Backend APIs are the most common kind of intern project. This proves you can design resources and status codes, model data in SQL, protect endpoints, and test a service the way a team would.
brief:
Build the backend for a small real product, for example a study-group planner, a club event board or a book-swap service. It needs users, at least two related resources with a one-to-many relationship (groups and their sessions) and one many-to-many relationship (members of groups).

Constraints: a relational database (PostgreSQL recommended, SQLite acceptable while developing) managed with migrations. Passwords hashed with a slow algorithm such as bcrypt or argon2, never stored in plain text. Token-based authentication (signed tokens such as JWTs, or opaque session tokens) on every write endpoint, plus authorization checks so users can change only their own resources. Input validation that returns 400 or 422 with a helpful body. Pagination on list endpoints. Correct status codes: 201 on create, 204 on delete, 401 versus 403, 404, and 409 on conflicts.

Testing is part of the spec: integration tests run against a real test database and cover the happy paths, validation errors and authorization failures. Package the API and database with Docker Compose so a reviewer can start everything with one command. The next project builds a frontend on this API, so design it with care.

milestones.title: Design first
tasks: List the resources and endpoints with request and response shapes (a short doc or an OpenAPI spec)
Draw the database schema with keys and relationships
Decide the status code for success and for each error case
milestones.doneWhen: A design doc in the repository lists every endpoint with its method, path, auth requirement and status codes.

milestones.title: Database and CRUD
tasks: Create tables with migrations, foreign keys and unique constraints
Implement create, read, update and delete for the main resources
Add pagination and filtering to list endpoints
milestones.doneWhen: Every CRUD endpoint works from curl, and list endpoints return one page plus a way to request the next.

milestones.title: Authentication and authorization
tasks: Sign-up and login with hashed passwords
Issue and verify tokens, and protect every write endpoint
Check ownership so users cannot edit or delete other users' resources
milestones.doneWhen: Tests show 401 without a token, 403 when editing someone else's resource, and success for the owner.

milestones.title: Validation and errors
tasks: Validate every input and return clear error messages
Use one consistent error format across all endpoints
Return 409, not 500, when a unique constraint is violated
milestones.doneWhen: No request you can craft by hand produces a 500 error or a stack trace in the response.

milestones.title: Tests and CI
tasks: Integration tests against a test database that is reset between tests
Cover happy paths, validation, authorization and pagination
Run the suite in GitHub Actions with a database service container
milestones.doneWhen: CI runs 40 or more tests on every push and is green.

milestones.title: Ship it
tasks: A Dockerfile and a Docker Compose file for the API and the database
A seed script with sample data
A README with setup, an endpoint overview and design decisions
milestones.doneWhen: A reviewer can run `docker compose up` and call the API with the README's examples without installing anything else.

stretch: Rate limiting on the login endpoint
Deploy to a free tier with a managed database
Load test one endpoint, then add an index that measurably speeds it up
rubric: A reviewer should see passwords hashed with bcrypt or argon2 and no secrets in the repository
A reviewer should see correct, consistent status codes, including 401 versus 403 and 409 on conflicts
A reviewer should see authorization checks that stop users changing others' data, proven by tests
A reviewer should see migrations plus foreign key and unique constraints in the schema
A reviewer should see parameterized queries or an ORM, never SQL built by string concatenation
A reviewer should see integration tests running in CI against a real database
A reviewer should be able to start the whole stack with one Docker Compose command
showcase: README: what the API is for, an endpoint table, the schema diagram, a Docker Compose quick start, example curl requests, design decisions and security notes
Link the generated OpenAPI docs page if your framework provides one
Show the CI badge and the test count at the top of the README
resumeBullet: Built a REST API (FastAPI, PostgreSQL) for a study-group planner with token auth, ownership checks and paginated endpoints; 60 integration tests run in GitHub Actions, and the stack starts with one Docker Compose command.
interviewTalkingPoints: How you modeled the many-to-many relationship and which indexes you added
401 versus 403, and how your tests prove authorization works
Why passwords need a slow hash, and what a salt protects against
How you kept tests isolated (a transaction per test or a fresh database)
What you would change to handle 100 times more traffic
